title: Throughput safeguard lease handoff and deferred eviction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem:
Redwood Dedicated customers require predictable per-tenant sustained throughput during maintenance windows and node lifecycle events. Current drain behavior can cause short-term throughput cliffs when hosts are evacuated concurrently, and KV cache cold starts amplify tail latency. We need a coordinated mechanism that preserves contract-level throughput while enabling safe node upgrades and maintenance with minimal manual intervention.

Proposal (summary):
Implement a throughput-safeguard lease handoff protocol with deferred eviction semantics and a lightweight preheat phase for KV caches. The orchestrator will: 1) allocate short-lived throughput leases to receiving hosts prior to drain, 2) defer eviction of select allocations until leases reach steady-state, 3) initiate targeted KV prewarm for warmed prefixes, and 4) expose autoscaler policy knobs to consume/return leases. This preserves SLOs during rolling maintenance and integrates with existing autoscaling and routing layers.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- No more than 5% degradation in p50/p95 token latency for customers with sustained throughput SLAs during a rolling maintenance event (measured across controlled canary).
- Throughput delta for SLA-bound tenants limited to <= 10% of provisioned capacity during handoff windows.
- Drains complete without causing global request failures; fallback to lower-tier model variant if local capacity cannot be hedged within 30s.
- Telemetry shows lease allocation/release events with correlated KV prewarm success/failure for each host.
- Feature controllable via fleet policy and per-customer override in console.

Design details:
1) Lease concept and lifecycle:
- A throughput lease is a soft contract granting an incoming host the right to accept up to X tokens/sec for a tenant while the source host drains. Leases have a TTL (e.g., 60–180s) and backoff on failure.
- When maintenance starts, the orchestrator computes handoff targets and creates leases against receiving hosts accounting for current load and reserved headroom.

2) Deferred eviction and grace windows:
- Instead of immediate eviction, we mark selected allocations as "deferred-evict" and allow in-flight requests to drain for a configurable grace window (default 45s).
- If a receiving host fails to reach steady state within the lease TTL, the orchestrator will either extend the lease (if pool has spare capacity) or trigger an automated fallback (traffic reroute to alternate region or model variant).

3) KV preheat strategy:
- Orchestrator triggers targeted KV prewarm against receiving hosts for the top-k prefixes observed in telemetry for each tenant. Prewarm has progressive concurrency and bails on high-latency signals.
- Prewarm outcomes recorded and surfaced in the console; failed prewarm marks tenant for conservative routing for the duration of the maintenance wave.

4) Autoscaler integration:
- Autoscaler exposes a "lease_headroom" parameter: minimum unallocated throughput to keep for lease assignments. The autoscaler will schedule scale-ups proactively when upcoming maintenance windows are detected.
- When leases are handed back, autoscaler rebalances to reclaim capacity.

5) Routing and fallback layers:
- Smart routing will prefer hosts with active leases and warmed KV state for SLA-bound tenants during handoff.
- Fallback chain: alternate host in same AZ -> alternate AZ -> degraded model variant. Each hop logs a structured fallback event for post-mortem.

Operational controls and console UX:
- New Console toggles: "Maintenance Mode" for a fleet wave with parameters (concurrency slice, max simultaneous leases, grace window).
- Per-tenant override: opt into conservative routing or immediate migration (for high-priority customers).
- Dashboard cards: ongoing lease allocations, prewarm success rate, anticipated throughput shortfall.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): internal tenants only, single AZ rollouts with synthetic traffic load and KV trace replay. Measure latency and throughput deltas and iterate on default TTLs and grace window.
- Stage 2 (opt-in customers): offer as beta for select Dedicated customers with monitored SLAs.
- Stage 3 (GA): enable by default, with safe defaults and an emergency kill-switch to disable leases per fleet.

Telemetry and SLO observability:
- New metrics: lease_allocated_total, lease_released_total, lease_extends_total, prewarm_success_ratio, deferred_evictions_active, tenant_throughput_ratio_during_handoff.
- Traces should annotate handoff events and any fallback hops. Dashboards to show correlated host-level KV hitrate and per-tenant latency curves.

Migration and compatibility:
- Backwards-compatible: hosts that do not implement prewarm or lease acceptance will be treated as prewarm-failed and receive conservative routing.
- Migration flagging: runtime-1.24 will include a feature flag to gate the orchestrator; gradual rollout controlled by fleet admin.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: lease over-allocation leading to contention. Mitigation: conservative default lease headroom and autoscaler prechecks before committing leases.
- Risk: KV prewarm amplifies load. Mitigation: progressive prewarm with latency-based abort and retry backoff.
- Risk: complex rollback during correlated failures. Mitigation: simple emergency disable path with automatic lease expiry and immediate traffic rebalancing.

Alternatives considered:
- Synchronous live-migration of allocations (rejected): too disruptive and increases tail latencies during migration.
- Global maintenance freeze (rejected): unacceptable for latency-sensitive SLAs.

Implementation plan (epics and tasks):
- Orchestrator core: lease allocation algorithm, state machine for lease lifecycle (ENG team).
- Router changes: lease-aware routing, fallback logging.
- Autoscaler hooks: headroom and proactive scaling signals.
- KV prewarm agent: lightweight prewarm API and telemetry.
- Console: controls and dashboards.
- E2E tests: load harness and chaos scenarios.

Estimated timeline: 6–8 weeks to canary, additional 4–6 weeks for opt-in beta and GA hardening.
